title: The Euler-Mascheroni Constant as a Gamma-Function Derivative: γ = -Γ'(1)
description: A machine-verified account of the identity γ = -Γ'(1) connecting the Euler-Mascheroni constant to the derivative of the Gamma function, discharging the second open question of the parent Euler-Mascheroni entry. The flagship identity is derived directly from Mathlib's Gamma-derivative library (Mathlib.NumberTheory.Harmonic.GammaDeriv); this entry adds the concrete evaluations, sign analysis, and bound transfer on top. Includes the general integer formula Γ'(n+1) = n!(-γ + H_n), concrete values Γ'(1) = -γ, Γ'(2) = 1 - γ, Γ'(3) = 3 - 2γ, the sign change Γ'(1) < 0 < Γ'(2) that locates the minimum of Γ between 1 and 2, a sharp enclosure -2/3 < Γ'(1) < -1/2 from the parent's bounds, and the half-integer derivative Γ'(1/2) = -√π(γ + 2 log 2).

overview.historicalContext:
The Euler-Mascheroni constant γ ≈ 0.57721566 has two classical faces. Euler (1734) defined it as the limiting gap γ = lim_{n→∞}(H_n − log n) between the harmonic numbers and the logarithm. Independently it is the derivative of the Gamma function at 1: γ = −Γ'(1), equivalently ψ(1) = −γ for the digamma function ψ = Γ'/Γ. This second characterization ties γ directly to the analytic theory of the Gamma function and to the values Γ'(n+1) = n!(−γ + H_n).

The parent entry (harmonic-divergence-oq-01) formalized the limit definition, bounds 1/2 < γ < 2/3, and Theisinger's theorem, but left the Gamma-derivative connection documented only in comments, believing the required Mathlib infrastructure was too costly to compile. This entry shows the Mathlib file Mathlib.NumberTheory.Harmonic.GammaDeriv compiles cheaply from cached oleans, and turns the documented identity into machine-verified theorems.
overview.problemStatement:
The parent entry's second open question asks: formalize the connection γ = −Γ'(1). This entry answers it, and develops the surrounding derivative theory:

1. γ = −Γ'(1) (the digamma value ψ(1) = −γ).
2. Γ'(n+1) = n!(−γ + H_n) for all n.
3. Concrete values: Γ'(1) = −γ, Γ'(2) = 1 − γ, Γ'(3) = 3 − 2γ.
4. Sign change Γ'(1) < 0 < Γ'(2): where does the minimum of Γ lie?
5. How tight an enclosure of Γ'(1) follows from 1/2 < γ < 2/3?
6. The half-integer value Γ'(1/2) = −√π(γ + 2 log 2).
overview.proofStrategy:
Every result delegates to Mathlib's GammaDeriv library and elementary arithmetic:

1. **Core identity**: `gamma_eq_neg_deriv_Gamma_one` wraps `Real.eulerMascheroniConstant_eq_neg_deriv`; `hasDerivAt_Gamma_one` wraps `Real.hasDerivAt_Gamma_one`.
2. **Integer formula**: `deriv_Gamma_nat` and `hasDerivAt_Gamma_nat` wrap `Real.deriv_Gamma_nat` / `Real.hasDerivAt_Gamma_nat`.
3. **Concrete values**: specialize the integer formula at n = 1, 2, compute the factorial and harmonic number with `norm_num [harmonic, Finset.sum_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_zero, Nat.factorial]`, and finish with `linarith`.
4. **Sign & bounds**: combine `deriv_Gamma_one`/`deriv_Gamma_two` with the parent's bounds `Real.one_half_lt_eulerMascheroniConstant` and `Real.eulerMascheroniConstant_lt_two_thirds` via `linarith`.
5. **Half-integer**: wrap `Real.hasDerivAt_Gamma_one_half`; negativity from √π > 0, log 2 > 0, γ > 0 via `nlinarith`.

A `#print axioms` audit confirms only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound are used — the entry is axiom-free in the project's sense.
keyInsights: γ has two classical faces that this entry welds together: Euler's (1734) limiting-gap definition γ = limₙ(Hₙ − log n) and the analytic characterization γ = −Γ′(1). The bridge is the digamma function ψ = Γ′/Γ, whose value ψ(1) = −γ makes the Euler–Mascheroni constant literally the logarithmic derivative of Γ at 1.

The general formula Γ′(n+1) = n!(−γ + Hₙ) shows the harmonic numbers Hₙ reappearing inside the Gamma derivative — the same Hₙ whose divergence defines γ. Setting n = 0 (H₀ = 0) recovers Γ′(1) = −γ; the factorial factor n! = Γ(n+1) reflects ψ(n+1) = −γ + Hₙ scaled by the value of Γ itself.

The sign change Γ′(1) = −γ < 0 < 1 − γ = Γ′(2) pins down qualitative behavior with no numerics beyond γ < 1: Γ is decreasing at 1 and increasing at 2, so its unique minimum on the positive reals lies strictly between 1 and 2 (in fact near 1.4616). A one-line consequence of two exact derivative values.

Numerical bounds transfer verbatim through the exact identity: the parent's machine-verified bracket 1/2 < γ < 2/3 becomes the sharp enclosure −2/3 < Γ′(1) < −1/2 with no additional analysis, because Γ′(1) = −γ is an equality, not an approximation.

The half-integer value Γ′(1/2) = −√π(γ + 2 log 2) exhibits how the reflection/duplication structure of Γ injects a log 2 term: it is ψ(1/2) = −γ − 2 log 2 multiplied by Γ(1/2) = √π. This is the derivative-level shadow of Γ(1/2) = √π and shows γ entangled with log 2 at half-integer arguments.

Formalization insight: the parent entry left this identity in comments believing the Gamma-derivative infrastructure was too costly to compile. The key realization here is that Mathlib.NumberTheory.Harmonic.GammaDeriv already provides ψ(1) = −γ and Γ′(n+1) = n!(−γ + Hₙ) and builds cheaply from cached oleans — turning a documented remark into verified theorems at low cost.

conclusion.summary: This entry converts the parent Euler-Mascheroni formalization's documented Gamma-function connection into fully machine-verified theorems: γ = −Γ'(1), the integer formula Γ'(n+1) = n!(−γ + H_n), concrete small-integer and half-integer values, sign analysis locating the minimum of Γ, and a sharp enclosure of Γ'(1).
conclusion.implications: The identity γ = −Γ'(1) is the bridge between the elementary (limit of H_n − log n) and analytic (digamma) theories of the Euler-Mascheroni constant. Formalizing it verified — and cheaply, contrary to the parent's expectation — makes the whole Gamma-derivative toolkit available to the gallery. The sign change Γ'(1) < 0 < Γ'(2) rigorously locates the well-known minimum of the Gamma function between 1 and 2.
openQuestions: Prove existence and uniqueness of the minimizer of Γ on (0,∞) (numerically ≈ 1.4616) by combining the sign change with continuity/convexity of Γ' on [1,2]
Formalize the digamma function ψ = Γ'/Γ explicitly and its values ψ(n) = −γ + H_{n−1}
Formalize the Laurent expansion lim_{s→1}(ζ(s) − 1/(s−1)) = γ (parent open question 3, requires ZetaAsymp)
Prove that γ is irrational (open since Euler, 1734)

sections.title: Overview: γ = -Γ'(1)
sections.description: Docstring and imports. Frames the entry as discharging the parent Euler–Mascheroni entry's second open question — identifying the Euler–Mascheroni constant γ as the negative derivative of the Gamma function at 1 — and states the results proved: the defining identity, its integer-argument generalization, and supporting positivity/monotonicity facts.

sections.title: The Defining Connection γ = -Γ'(1)
sections.description: The central identity: `gamma_eq_neg_deriv_Gamma_one` states γ = −Γ'(1), `hasDerivAt_Gamma_one` gives HasDerivAt Gamma (−γ) 1, and `deriv_Gamma_one` extracts deriv Gamma 1 = −γ. This is exactly the parent entry's second open question, delegated to Mathlib's `eulerMascheroniConstant_eq_neg_deriv` and `hasDerivAt_Gamma_one`.

sections.title: The Integer Formula Γ'(n+1) = n!(-γ + H_n)
sections.description: The general formula for the derivative of Γ at every positive integer in terms of harmonic numbers and γ, as both a `deriv` equation (`deriv_Gamma_nat`) and a `HasDerivAt` statement (`hasDerivAt_Gamma_nat`). Delegates to Mathlib's `Real.deriv_Gamma_nat`.

sections.title: Concrete Values Γ'(2) = 1 - γ and Γ'(3) = 3 - 2γ
sections.description: Specializes the integer formula at n = 1 and n = 2. Since 1! = 1, H_1 = 1, one gets Γ'(2) = 1 − γ; since 2! = 2, H_2 = 3/2, one gets Γ'(3) = 3 − 2γ. Proved by computing the factorial and harmonic value with norm_num and finishing with linarith.

sections.title: Sign Analysis and the Minimum of Γ
sections.description: From γ > 0 we get Γ'(1) < 0, and from γ < 2/3 < 1 we get Γ'(2) > 0. The packaged statement `deriv_Gamma_sign_change` records Γ'(1) < 0 < Γ'(2). Since Γ is smooth on (0,∞), this sign change is the analytic signature of the unique minimum of Γ, which therefore lies strictly between 1 and 2 (numerically near 1.4616).

sections.title: Sharp Enclosure of Γ'(1) from 1/2 < γ < 2/3
sections.description: Transfers the parent entry's enclosure 1/2 < γ < 2/3 through the identity Γ'(1) = −γ to obtain −2/3 < Γ'(1) < −1/2, a machine-verified numerical bracket for the derivative.

sections.title: The Half-Integer Derivative Γ'(1/2)
sections.description: The value Γ'(1/2) = −√π(γ + 2 log 2), obtained via the Gamma duplication formula (`hasDerivAt_Gamma_one_half` and `deriv_Gamma_one_half`), together with its negativity `deriv_Gamma_one_half_neg`, proved from √π > 0, log 2 > 0, and γ > 0.

crossReferences.description: This entry discharges the second open question of the parent Euler-Mascheroni entry — the connection γ = −Γ'(1) — which the parent documented only as a comment, believing the Gamma-derivative infrastructure too costly to compile.
The grandparent entry establishes harmonic series divergence and basic harmonic-number properties; the harmonic numbers H_n reappear here as the values Γ'(n+1)/n! + γ.
Both entries concern special values connected to the Riemann zeta function; γ is the constant term of the Laurent expansion of ζ at s=1, and appears in the Gamma-function machinery underlying ζ.
